blogPosts.title: How Much Does Bathroom Tiling Cost in Croydon, VIC?
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a bathroom reno in Croydon? We break down tile costs, labour rates, and what affects your final price in Melbourne's eastern suburbs.
body: If you are a Croydon homeowner thinking about a bathroom renovation, one of the first questions on your mind is probably what it will actually cost to tile the space. In Melbourne's eastern suburbs, bathroom tiling costs can vary widely depending on the tiles you choose, the size of your bathroom, and the complexity of the layout. At Instagram Tiling, we have been fitting tiles across Croydon and surrounding suburbs like Mooroolbark, Ringwood, and Kilsyth for years, and we know the local pricing inside out. A standard Croydon bathroom tiling project typically starts from around $65 per square metre for basic ceramic tiles, but premium porcelain or natural stone can push that figure significantly higher. Understanding what drives these costs helps you plan your renovation budget with confidence and avoid nasty surprises down the track.

The tiles themselves make up a significant portion of your total bathroom tiling budget, and the price range is enormous. Budget ceramic tiles suitable for a Croydon bathroom can be found for as little as $25 to $50 per square metre, offering decent durability and a clean finish for guest bathrooms or investment properties. Mid-range porcelain tiles, which are extremely popular in Croydon homes, typically cost between $60 and $120 per square metre and offer superior water resistance and wear characteristics. If you are after something truly premium, natural stone tiles like travertine, marble, or slate can cost anywhere from $100 to $300 per square metre or more. For a typical Croydon bathroom measuring around 6 to 8 square metres, your tile material costs alone could range from $300 on the budget end to well over $2,000 for premium stone. We always recommend visiting Croydon tile showrooms in person to see and feel the tiles before committing, as photos rarely capture the true texture and colour variation.

Labour is the other major cost component when it comes to bathroom tiling in Croydon, and it is where the skill and experience of your tiler really matters. In Melbourne's eastern suburbs, professional tiling labour typically runs between $45 and $80 per square metre, depending on the complexity of the job and the tiler's experience level. Simple, straightforward wall tiling with standard-sized tiles will naturally cost less per square metre than intricate mosaic work or large-format tiles that require precision cuts and levelling systems. At Instagram Tiling, we quote our bathroom tiling jobs on a project basis rather than hourly, so Croydon homeowners know exactly what they are paying before we start. This transparent approach means no hidden charges and no bill shock when the job is finished. Most standard Croydon bathroom tiling projects take between three and five days from demolition to completion, depending on the scope of work involved.

The size and layout of your Croydon bathroom has a major impact on the overall tiling cost, and it is something many homeowners do not fully appreciate until they get their first quote. A compact ensuite with a simple layout might only need 15 to 20 square metres of tile coverage across the floor and walls, while a large main bathroom with a freestanding tub, separate shower, and floor-to-ceiling tiling could require 30 square metres or more. Croydon homes built in the 1970s and 1980s often have smaller, more compartmentalised bathrooms that can actually keep tiling costs down, while newer builds in the area tend to feature larger, open-plan bathrooms. The shape of the room also matters significantly, as bathrooms with lots of corners, recesses, or angled walls require more cuts and more time, which translates directly into higher labour costs. When we provide a free quote for Croydon homeowners, we measure everything precisely so the price we quote is the price you pay.

Beyond the tiles and labour, there are several additional costs that Croydon homeowners need to factor into their bathroom tiling budget. Waterproofing is a mandatory requirement under Australian Standard AS 3740, and it typically adds $500 to $1,000 to your project depending on the size of the wet area. Quality waterproofing is absolutely essential in Croydon homes, especially given Melbourne's variable climate with cold, wet winters that can exacerbate moisture issues. Grout selection is another consideration, as standard cement-based grout is the most affordable option but epoxy grout offers superior stain and mould resistance at a higher price point. Underfloor heating is increasingly popular in Croydon bathrooms, adding roughly $100 to $150 per square metre but providing wonderful comfort during those chilly Melbourne winter mornings. Other potential extras include tile removal and disposal, which typically costs $15 to $25 per square metre, and any substrate repair work that might be needed before new tiles can be laid.

Australian building standards play a critical role in bathroom tiling, and any Croydon tiler you hire should be fully across the relevant regulations. The Building Code of Australia and Australian Standard AS 3958.1 set out the requirements for tile installation in wet areas, including minimum adhesive coverage, grout joint widths, and waterproofing requirements. In Victoria, bathroom waterproofing must be carried out by a licensed professional and a compliance certificate must be issued upon completion. This is not just a formality, it protects you as a homeowner and is essential for insurance purposes and any future property sale. At Instagram Tiling, we ensure every Croydon bathroom project meets or exceeds these standards, giving you complete peace of mind. We also work closely with local Croydon building inspectors and can coordinate with your builder if the tiling is part of a larger renovation project.

Getting the best value for your bathroom tiling in Croydon is not just about finding the cheapest quote, it is about finding a tiler who delivers quality workmanship that will last for decades. A poorly tiled bathroom can develop cracked tiles, grout failure, and waterproofing issues that cost far more to fix than the original installation. We always recommend Croydon homeowners get at least three quotes, check that the tiler is fully licensed and insured, and ask to see examples of previous bathroom work in the local area. At Instagram Tiling, we are happy to show Croydon homeowners our portfolio of completed bathroom projects and provide references from local clients. For a free, no-obligation quote on your Croydon bathroom tiling project, give us a call or send us an email. We service Croydon, Mooroolbark, Ringwood, Kilsyth, Lilydale, and all surrounding eastern suburbs.

blogPosts.title: Best Floor Tiles for Melbourne's Eastern Suburbs Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing floor tiles for your Croydon home? Discover the best options for durability, style, and climate suitability in Melbourne's eastern suburbs.
body: Choosing the right floor tiles for your home in Melbourne's eastern suburbs is about more than just aesthetics, it is about finding a product that can handle the local climate, lifestyle demands, and the everyday wear and tear of Australian family life. Croydon, situated at the foothills of the Dandenong Ranges, experiences a climate that ranges from hot, dry summers to cool, damp winters with occasional frost, and your floor tiles need to perform well across all these conditions. At Instagram Tiling, we have extensive experience helping Croydon and Mooroolbark homeowners select floor tiles that look stunning and stand the test of time. Whether you are tiling a high-traffic kitchen, a cosy living area, or a moisture-prone bathroom, the right tile selection makes all the difference. In this guide, we will walk you through the best floor tile options for homes across Melbourne's eastern suburbs.

Porcelain tiles are overwhelmingly the most popular choice for floor tiling in Croydon homes, and for very good reason. Porcelain is incredibly dense and durable, with a water absorption rate of less than 0.5 percent, making it ideal for everything from kitchens and living rooms to bathrooms and laundries. Modern porcelain tiles come in an astonishing range of finishes, including realistic timber-look planks, concrete-look slabs, and natural stone reproductions that are virtually indistinguishable from the real thing. For Croydon families with children and pets, porcelain floor tiles offer excellent scratch resistance and are extremely easy to clean and maintain. Prices for quality porcelain floor tiles in the Croydon area typically range from $40 to $120 per square metre, with premium designer collections commanding higher prices. We generally recommend rectified porcelain tiles for Croydon floor installations, as their precise edges allow for narrower grout lines and a more seamless, contemporary finish.

Natural stone tiles bring a warmth and character to Croydon homes that is difficult to replicate with manufactured tiles, and they remain a popular choice for homeowners seeking a premium, timeless look. Travertine is particularly well-suited to Melbourne's eastern suburbs, with its warm, earthy tones complementing the leafy, established gardens that Croydon is known for. Marble floor tiles create an unmistakable sense of luxury and work beautifully in formal entryways and living areas. Slate tiles, with their natural texture and slip resistance, are an excellent option for Croydon homes with indoor-outdoor flow, as they handle wet conditions well and hide dirt effectively. However, natural stone does require more maintenance than porcelain, including regular sealing to prevent staining and moisture absorption. For Croydon homeowners considering natural stone floor tiles, we recommend budgeting between $80 and $250 per square metre for the tiles themselves, plus additional costs for sealing and ongoing maintenance products.

One of the biggest trends we are seeing in Croydon floor tiling is the growing popularity of large-format tiles, which create a striking, modern look with fewer grout lines and a more expansive feel. Tiles measuring 600 by 600 millimetres and above, including the increasingly popular 800 by 800 millimetre format, are transforming Croydon living spaces and kitchens with their clean, minimalist aesthetic. Large-format tiles work particularly well in open-plan areas, which are common in newer Croydon homes and renovations, as they create a visual continuity that makes spaces feel larger and more connected. However, it is worth noting that large-format tiles require a perfectly level substrate and skilled installation, as any imperfections in the floor will be more visible. Timber-look plank tiles, typically measuring 200 by 1200 millimetres or larger, are another major trend in Croydon homes, offering the warmth and beauty of timber flooring with the durability and low maintenance of porcelain. These are especially popular in Croydon homes transitioning between indoor and outdoor entertaining areas.

The slip rating of your floor tiles is a critical consideration that many Croydon homeowners overlook, but it has a direct impact on safety, particularly in wet areas. Australian Standard AS 4586 classifies tile slip resistance into several categories, and for Croydon bathrooms and laundries, you should look for tiles with a minimum P3 rating for wet barefoot areas. For Croydon kitchens and entryways where shoes are worn and water may be tracked in, a P2 or P3 rating is generally appropriate. Outdoor tiles for Croydon patios, pool surrounds, and Alfresco areas need a higher slip rating, typically P4 or P5, to ensure adequate grip even when wet. At Instagram Tiling, we help Croydon homeowners navigate these specifications to ensure their floor tiles are not only beautiful but also safe and compliant with Australian standards. Getting the slip rating wrong can be a costly mistake and potentially a liability issue, so it is well worth discussing with an experienced Croydon tiler before making your final selection.

When budgeting for floor tiling in your Croydon home, it is important to consider the total installed cost rather than just the per-square-metre price of the tiles. A realistic budget for quality floor tiling in Croydon, including tiles, adhesive, grout, labour, and preparation work, typically ranges from $80 to $200 per square metre for standard ceramic and porcelain options. Premium natural stone or designer porcelain installations can push the total cost to $250 per square metre or more. For a typical Croydon home looking to tile an open-plan kitchen and living area of around 30 to 40 square metres, you should expect to invest somewhere between $2,500 and $8,000 depending on your tile selection. At Instagram Tiling, we provide detailed, itemised quotes for all Croydon floor tiling projects so you can see exactly where your money is going. We also offer flexible payment options to help Croydon homeowners spread the cost of larger tiling projects without compromising on quality or materials.

Choosing the right floor tiles for your Croydon home is a decision that will impact your daily life for years to come, and it is worth taking the time to get it right. We always recommend Croydon homeowners visit local tile showrooms to see tiles in person, as colours and textures can look very different on screen compared to real life. Bring samples home and view them in the actual lighting conditions of your Croydon space, as natural and artificial light can dramatically alter how a tile appears. At Instagram Tiling, we are always happy to provide on-site consultations for Croydon homeowners, helping you select floor tiles that suit your space, lifestyle, and budget. Whether you are building a new home in Croydon, renovating an existing property, or simply updating a single room, our team has the expertise and local knowledge to deliver exceptional floor tiling results. Contact us today for a free measure and quote at your Croydon property.

blogPosts.title: Outdoor Tiling in Croydon: A Complete Guide to Patios and Alfresco Areas
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning outdoor tiling in Croydon? Learn about the best materials, Melbourne climate considerations, and costs for patios and Alfresco areas.
body: Outdoor tiling is one of the best investments a Croydon homeowner can make, transforming underused patios and courtyards into stunning entertaining spaces that add genuine value to your property. Melbourne's eastern suburbs enjoy a climate that is well-suited to outdoor living, with long, warm summers and mild autumns that make an outdoor entertaining area an extension of your home for much of the year. Croydon, with its generous block sizes and established gardens, offers the perfect canvas for beautifully tiled outdoor spaces that blend seamlessly with the natural surroundings. At Instagram Tiling, we specialise in outdoor tiling for Croydon homes, from intimate courtyard transformations to large-scale patio installations that become the centrepiece of your outdoor lifestyle. Whether you are planning a new outdoor tiled area or looking to replace tired, outdated pavers, this guide covers everything Croydon homeowners need to know about outdoor tiling, including material selection, climate considerations, and cost expectations.

Selecting the right tiles for your Croydon outdoor area is crucial, as they need to withstand Melbourne's harsh and unpredictable climate while maintaining their appearance and structural integrity. Porcelain tiles are the most popular choice for Croydon outdoor areas, thanks to their exceptional durability, low water absorption rate, and resistance to fading from UV exposure. For Croydon patios and Alfresco areas, we recommend choosing porcelain tiles specifically rated for outdoor use, with a slip resistance of P3 or higher to ensure safety when the surface is wet. Terracotta tiles offer a classic, Mediterranean aesthetic that suits many established Croydon homes, particularly those with traditional or Tuscan-inspired architecture. Natural stone options like bluestone and sandstone are also popular in Croydon outdoor spaces, providing a natural, organic look that complements the area's leafy character. Whatever material you choose, ensure it is rated for external use and compatible with Melbourne's freeze-thaw cycles, which can cause inferior tiles to crack or delaminate.

Melbourne's climate presents specific challenges for outdoor tiling in Croydon that homeowners need to be aware of before starting their project. Croydon experiences temperature extremes that can range from over 40 degrees Celsius during summer heatwaves to below freezing on cold winter mornings, and this thermal cycling puts significant stress on outdoor tiles and their adhesive beds. Proper substrate preparation is essential for outdoor tiling in Croydon, as any movement or inadequacy in the base will quickly lead to cracked tiles or loose paving. We typically recommend a reinforced concrete slab for Croydon outdoor tiled areas, as it provides the most stable and long-lasting foundation. Waterproofing and drainage are also critical considerations, particularly given Croydon's position near the Dandenong Ranges, which means the area can receive higher rainfall than suburbs closer to the bay. Adequate fall towards drainage points, typically a minimum of 1 in 80, prevents water pooling and protects both the tiles and the underlying structure.

The cost of outdoor tiling in Croydon varies significantly depending on the size of the area, the tiles you choose, and the complexity of the preparation and installation work required. For a standard Croydon patio of around 20 to 30 square metres, outdoor porcelain tiles will typically cost between $50 and $120 per square metre, with installation adding another $60 to $90 per square metre. Premium natural stone options like bluestone or travertine can push the per-square-metre cost to $150 or more for materials alone. Site preparation, which may include old paver removal, levelling, and concrete work, can add $1,000 to $3,000 to your project depending on the current state of the area. For a typical Croydon outdoor tiling project, homeowners should budget between $3,000 and $10,000 for a complete transformation, depending on the scope and material choices. At Instagram Tiling, we provide detailed, fixed-price quotes for all Croydon outdoor tiling projects, so you know exactly what your investment will be before we break ground.

One of the most important aspects of outdoor tiling in Croydon is ensuring proper drainage and waterproofing to protect your investment from Melbourne's variable weather. A well-designed outdoor tiled area in Croydon should incorporate adequate falls to direct water away from the house and towards appropriate drainage points, preventing standing water that can cause slips, staining, and long-term structural damage. For raised outdoor areas and balconies in Croydon homes, a waterproof membrane beneath the tiles is essential to prevent water ingress into the structure below. We also recommend incorporating expansion joints in larger Croydon outdoor tiled areas, as these allow for thermal movement without cracking the tiles. The grout you choose for outdoor tiling in Croydon also matters significantly. We recommend using a high-quality, polymer-modified grout that is more resistant to cracking, staining, and the effects of weather exposure compared to standard cement-based grout. These technical details might seem minor, but they are the difference between an outdoor tiled area that lasts decades and one that needs costly repairs within a few years.

Planning your Croydon outdoor tiling project with the right timeline is important, as Melbourne's seasonal weather patterns can affect both the installation process and the curing of adhesives and grouts. The best time for outdoor tiling in Croydon is during the drier months from October to April, when consistent temperatures and lower rainfall provide ideal conditions for tile installation and adhesive curing. We generally avoid undertaking outdoor tiling projects in Croydon during the depth of winter, as temperatures below 10 degrees can compromise adhesive performance and extend curing times significantly. Summer installations in Croydon need to account for extreme heat, as temperatures above 35 degrees can cause adhesives to dry too quickly, potentially weakening the bond. At Instagram Tiling, we carefully monitor weather conditions for all our Croydon outdoor tiling projects and adjust our scheduling to ensure optimal installation conditions. This attention to detail is one of the reasons our outdoor tiled areas across Croydon continue to look great and perform well year after year.

Investing in quality outdoor tiling for your Croydon home is about more than just aesthetics, it is about creating a functional, durable outdoor living space that your family can enjoy for years to come. A well-tiled outdoor area in Croydon adds genuine property value, with real estate data consistently showing that quality outdoor entertaining spaces are among the most sought-after features for buyers in Melbourne's eastern suburbs. At Instagram Tiling, we have completed hundreds of outdoor tiling projects across Croydon, Mooroolbark, Ringwood, and surrounding suburbs, and we understand what works best in the local environment. From initial design consultation through to final grouting and sealing, we manage every aspect of your Croydon outdoor tiling project to ensure a seamless, stress-free experience. If you are ready to transform your Croydon outdoor space, contact us today for a free on-site consultation and detailed quote. We will visit your property, discuss your ideas and requirements, and provide honest, expert advice on the best outdoor tiling solutions for your Croydon home and budget.

blogPosts.title: Kitchen Splashback Tiling Trends for Croydon Homeowners in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Explore the latest kitchen splashback tiling trends for Croydon homes, from subway classics to bold large-format porcelain panels.
body: The kitchen splashback is one of the most visible and impactful design elements in any Croydon home, and choosing the right tiles for this feature can completely transform the look and feel of your kitchen. In Melbourne's eastern suburbs, kitchen renovations have become increasingly popular, and the splashback is where homeowners can make a bold design statement without the expense of a full kitchen overhaul. Croydon homes, ranging from classic 1970s builds to contemporary new constructions, each offer unique opportunities for splashback tiling that reflects the homeowner's personal style while complementing the existing kitchen design. At Instagram Tiling, we have been creating stunning kitchen splashbacks for Croydon homeowners for years, and we have seen the trends evolve dramatically. In this guide, we explore the most popular kitchen splashback tiling trends for Croydon homes in 2026, providing inspiration and practical advice for homeowners planning a kitchen refresh.

Subway tiles remain one of the most enduringly popular choices for kitchen splashbacks in Croydon homes, and their appeal shows no signs of fading. The classic rectangular subway tile, typically in a clean white finish, provides a timeless backdrop that works with virtually any kitchen style, from traditional to ultra-modern. However, Croydon homeowners are increasingly exploring creative variations on the classic subway format, including coloured subway tiles in shades of sage green, dusty blue, and warm terracotta that reflect the natural landscape of Melbourne's eastern suburbs. The laying pattern is another way Croydon homeowners are adding personality to their subway tile splashbacks, with herringbone, vertical stack, and offset brick patterns all trending strongly. Larger format subway tiles, measuring 100 by 300 millimetres or even 100 by 400 millimetres, are becoming increasingly popular in Croydon kitchens, offering a more contemporary, streamlined look with fewer grout lines. Price-wise, subway tiles represent excellent value for Croydon homeowners, with most options available for $30 to $80 per square metre.

Large-format tiles and porcelain panels are dramatically reshaping kitchen splashback design in Croydon, offering a sleek, grout-free appearance that is particularly striking in modern kitchens. These oversized tiles, some measuring up to 1600 by 3200 millimetres, can cover an entire splashback area with just one or two pieces, creating a seamless, minimalist look that is both visually stunning and incredibly easy to clean. For Croydon homeowners with open-plan kitchens, large-format porcelain panels create a sense of continuity and space that smaller tiles simply cannot achieve. The range of finishes available in large-format tiles is remarkable, with realistic marble reproductions, concrete looks, and even timber-effect options all available for splashback applications. Installation of large-format tiles requires specialist skills and equipment, as the tiles are extremely heavy and require precise handling and cutting. At Instagram Tiling, we have invested in the training and equipment necessary to install large-format splashback tiles for Croydon homeowners, ensuring every panel is perfectly positioned and securely bonded. While the material and installation costs are higher than traditional tiles, the result is a kitchen splashback that is truly spectacular.

Textured and three-dimensional tiles are emerging as a major trend for Croydon kitchen splashbacks in 2026, adding depth, interest, and a tactile quality that flat tiles cannot provide. Geometric patterned tiles, including hexagons, diamonds, and Moroccan-inspired designs, are being used by Croydon homeowners to create feature splashbacks that serve as the focal point of the entire kitchen. These textured tiles catch the light beautifully, creating shadows and visual depth that change throughout the day, adding a dynamic quality to the kitchen space. In Croydon homes with natural light from north-facing windows, textured splashback tiles can create stunning light effects that transform the kitchen atmosphere from morning to evening. The colour palette for textured splashback tiles in Croydon tends toward muted, earthy tones that complement the natural landscape of Melbourne's eastern suburbs, though bold monochromatic choices in black or deep navy are also gaining traction. When selecting textured tiles for a Croydon kitchen splashback, consider the practical implications, as some textured surfaces can be more challenging to clean than smooth tiles. Our team at Instagram Tiling can advise Croydon homeowners on textured tile options that balance visual impact with practical maintainability.

Colour is playing an increasingly important role in Croydon kitchen splashback design, with homeowners moving away from safe neutrals toward more expressive, personalised palettes. Deep greens inspired by the Dandenong Ranges forests that frame Croydon are proving particularly popular, as are warm terracotta and rust tones that evoke the Australian landscape. These nature-inspired colours connect Croydon kitchens to their surroundings and create a sense of warmth and authenticity that resonates with the area's community character. For Croydon homeowners who prefer a more dramatic look, dark and moody splashback tiles in charcoal, deep blue, or black are being paired with lighter cabinetry to create striking contrast and visual drama. Alternatively, patterned encaustic-style tiles are making a strong comeback in Croydon kitchens, offering intricate designs that add personality and character. When choosing splashback tile colours for your Croydon kitchen, consider how they interact with your benchtop, cabinetry, and flooring, as well as the direction and intensity of natural light in the space. At Instagram Tiling, we offer colour consultation as part of our Croydon kitchen splashback service, helping homeowners navigate the vast array of options to find the perfect combination.

The practical aspects of kitchen splashback tiling are just as important as the aesthetic considerations, and Croydon homeowners need to think carefully about functionality alongside style. Behind the cooktop, your splashback tiles will be exposed to heat, grease splatter, and steam on a daily basis, so durability and ease of cleaning are paramount. Smooth, glazed porcelain tiles are the most practical choice for this high-exposure zone, as their non-porous surface wipes clean easily and resists staining from cooking oils and sauces. The area around the kitchen sink also requires tiles that can handle frequent water exposure, and proper waterproofing behind the tiles is essential to prevent moisture damage to the wall substrate. In Croydon homes, where many kitchens open onto dining and living areas, the splashback tiles need to transition visually between functional and social spaces, which is where careful design planning pays off. Grout selection for kitchen splashbacks in Croydon is another practical consideration that impacts both appearance and maintenance. Epoxy grout, while more expensive than standard cement-based grout, offers superior stain resistance and does not require sealing, making it an excellent choice for busy Croydon kitchens.

Planning and budgeting for a kitchen splashback tiling project in Croydon requires careful consideration of several cost factors, but it remains one of the most cost-effective ways to refresh your kitchen's appearance. Material costs for kitchen splashback tiles in Croydon typically range from $30 to $150 per square metre, depending on the tile type, brand, and design complexity. Most standard Croydon kitchen splashbacks cover between 3 and 6 square metres, so tile material costs alone generally fall between $100 and $900.
